title: Tuga A6 vs Tuga A8: Pocket Handheld or 8 Inch Rugged Tablet?
description: Tuga A6 handheld or Tuga A8 tablet, £80 apart. Pay more for the 8 inch screen and van mount, or keep the £80 for 5G, IP69K and a night vision camera.
summary: The A6 is £80 cheaper, pocketable, better sealed and has 5G; the A8 is the one if you fill in forms or read drawings on site, or want a tablet on the van dashboard.
lede: Buy the Tuga A6 at £299 for photos, job sheets and sign-off from a pocket; pay £80 more for the Tuga A8 at £379 if you fill in forms, read drawings or want a van mount. Both are rugged Android devices for sole traders and small firms.
verdict: The A6 costs £299 and the A8 £379, a gap of £80, and what that £80 buys is size. Both run Android 14, both are sealed to IP68 and drop tested to MIL-STD-810H, both have glove mode, NFC and GPS, and both are rated to work from -20°C to 60°C. The decision comes down to two things: how much screen your work needs, and whether you want to carry a tablet at all.

Pay the £80 for the screen. The A8 is 8 inches against 6.78, which helps with test schedules, long checklists and PDF drawings without pinching and zooming. It is 800 nits against 560, and the A8 is the one listed as sunlight readable for a bright roof. It also has USB-A, a hand strap in the box and the £109 Vehicle Mounting Dock, which is listed for the A8 and not the A6. The cost is weight: at 680g against 441g, it suits a bag or a van door pocket better than a trouser pocket.

Keep the £80 if a phone-sized screen will do. The A6 has 5G, IP69K, a larger battery with 33W fast charging, 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage, and a 64MP night vision camera for lofts, voids and under floors. A fingerprint sensor and face unlock are listed for the A6, not listed for the A8. Only the A6 has a paid 3-Year Warranty option, at £65; the A8 has the included 12 months. See the electricians page and the field service page, or tell us what you fill in on site and we will say which we would buy.
chooseA: You want one device that goes in a pocket or a Belt Holster (£22) rather than a tablet in a bag: 441g against 680g.
Your day is photos, job sheets, proof of delivery and sign-off, and a 6.78 inch screen at 2460 x 1080 is enough for that.
The device gets jet washed along with your kit: IP68 plus IP69K against IP68 alone on the A8.
You photograph lofts, voids and under floors, where the 64MP night vision camera is meant to earn its keep.
You upload from site and want 5G rather than 4G LTE, with 33W fast charging to top up between jobs.
chooseB: You fill in forms, test schedules or long checklists on site and want 8 inches of screen rather than pinching and zooming on 6.78.
You read drawings, PDFs or route maps on the device, where screen area matters more than pixel count.
You want it on the dashboard: the A8 is vehicle mountable and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) is listed for it, the A6 is not.
You work on bright roofs and open sites and want the 800 nit screen against 560 nits.
You plug in USB-A peripherals without an adapter: the A8 has USB-C and USB-A ports, the A6 has USB-C OTG.

faq.q: Is the Tuga A8 worth £80 more than the A6?
faq.a: Mostly for the screen. If you fill in forms, test schedules or checklists on site, or read drawings and PDFs, the 8 inch screen is worth £80 on its own, and the vehicle mount option and 800 nit brightness come with it. If your work is photos, short job sheets, proof of delivery and messaging, the A6 at £299 is the better buy, and it fits in a pocket. The A8 is the bigger device, and for forms and drawings bigger is what you are paying for.

faq.q: Can I do forms on the A6 instead of buying a tablet?
faq.a: Short ones should be fine, but check your own app first. The A6 screen is 6.78 inches at 2460 x 1080, a phone-sized screen suited to short job sheets and signatures. Long forms and drawings mean a lot of scrolling, pinching and zooming, which is where the A8 starts to pay for itself. Check your own app on the device rather than assuming: open the longest form you fill in on a typical day and see whether you can work through it one-handed. The Capacitive Stylus (£14.99) is listed for the A8 but not for the A6, which matters if you want a stylus for customer signatures.

faq.q: Which is tougher, the A6 or the A8?
faq.a: They are close, and the A6 edges it on sealing. Both are IP68, both are drop tested to MIL-STD-810H and both are rated to work from -20°C to 60°C. The A6 adds IP69K, listed as surviving jet washing, not just rain, and lists Gorilla Glass 5, which is not listed for the A8. Neither lists a drop height. If the device will be jet washed, the A6 is the one rated for it. Our IP rating guide and MIL-STD-810H guide explain what each rating does and does not test.

faq.q: Can I mount the A6 in the van like the A8?
faq.a: Not with the same dock. The A8 is vehicle mountable and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109), a locking VESA mount with DC power input, is listed for the A8, A10, W8 and W10. It is not listed for the A6. What fits the A6 is the Car Phone Mount (£17), a heavy duty suction cup mount for rugged handhelds, and the 12V DC Car Charger (£26) fits both. So the A6 can sit in a suction cup mount and charge from the 12V socket, but if you want a locked-in dashboard unit that comes out as the site tablet, that is the A8. Everything is on the accessories page.
